observation_summary: The BrentSolver throws an IllegalArgumentException when one of the function endpoints is a root (value is 0), because the existing logic only checks if the signs are different and fails if they are not, even if one endpoint is already the solution.
reasoning_summary: The fix involves adding conditional checks (if-else blocks) to validate if either endpoint is close to zero (a root) before throwing the exception. This is a classic case of missing guard logic for boundary conditions, which falls under the 'Checking' category.
evidence_used: The fix adds 'if (Math.abs(yMin) <= functionValueAccuracy)' and 'if (yMin == 0.0)' checks.
The original code only checked 'if (sign >= 0)' and threw an exception, failing to account for cases where an endpoint is a root.
The bug report explicitly states: 'The exception should not be thrown... the algorithm should stop and return 0 as the root'.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the fix modifies the flow, the root cause is the absence of a check for the boundary condition (root at endpoint), not a flaw in the core root-finding algorithm itself.
